headings.title: SMTO-BOOT-0023 — The installer couldn't work out which vLLM version to install

html:
SMTO-BOOT-0023 — The installer couldn't work out which vLLM version to install

GUID: caa40dbf-f817-40e4-9e64-f4af06f32245
Slug: boot-model-install-plan-invalid
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The installer asks a helper file which vLLM version fits your computer, but the answer came back incomplete. It stopped before installing vLLM. The new Conda environment it had just created is still there, without vLLM.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure install-vllm.sh and vllm_install_support.py in the src/vllm folder come from the same SMTO copy. If you copied the installer elsewhere, copy both files together. The installer expects a three-line answer from this helper; a helper from another version can answer differently.
  2. Run conda env list and check that the environment from this attempt is listed; it was created but doesn't contain vLLM yet. Knowing it exists tells you the next attempt needs a different name or a clean start.
  3. Run the installer again with a new environment name, or first remove the half-built one with conda env remove --name followed by its name. The installer refuses names that already exist, so the half-built environment would block a retry with the same name.

What success looks like

  • The installer prints "Selected vLLM" with a version and CUDA backend, installs it, and ends with "vLLM installation complete".

If it still fails

  • Copy the full terminal output, including the SMTO-BOOT-0023 line, the lines just above it and the Error reference line, and send it to the person who maintains your SMTO copy. Don't pick a vLLM or CUDA version by hand to get around this; a wrong combination may not work with your graphics card.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • install-vllm.sh rejected the output of vllm_install_support.py plan because it was not exactly three lines (version, requirement, PyTorch CUDA backend); the new environment and its packaging tools already exist, but vLLM was not installed.

What this means

  • The wheel-planning helper output does not split into the three expected installation-plan lines. A new environment and its packaging tools may already exist. The malformed three-line plan is rejected before the selected vLLM installation command. The malformed output does not identify a safe wheel, CUDA backend or upstream version to substitute.

Why this can happen

  • The wheel-planning helper output does not split into the three expected installation-plan lines.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect matching helper/installer versions and the retained planning output.

How to fix it

  • Make sure install-vllm.sh and vllm_install_support.py come from the same checkout, and check that nothing in the new environment writes extra lines to stdout when the helper's plan command runs under conda run. Then remove the partially created environment or use a new name before reinstalling; do not substitute a guessed wheel, CUDA backend or vLLM version.
  • Preserve the installer diagnostics and use a supported installer/runtime version. Do not guess a wheel or CUDA combination.

Retry and execution caution

  • Repair the installer/helper mismatch, inspect the partial environment, then verify it or choose an unused environment name for a fresh install.

How to verify the fix

  • The matching helper returns three lines: release version, package requirement and CUDA backend; final environment verification then passes.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • A new environment and its packaging tools may already exist. The malformed three-line plan is rejected before the selected vLLM installation command.
  • The malformed output does not identify a safe wheel, CUDA backend or upstream version to substitute.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
